title: Runoff per unit rain fell in a 1997-1998 step in Victoria but declined from the 1950s in New South Wales; the Victorian step came before most water-table fall (CAMELS-AUS, 1952-2021)
abstract: Question: after 1997, south-east Australian runoff stayed 20-25% below its 1951-1996 rainfall-runoff relation. A drought-triggered cause, such as stream disconnection from falling groundwater, must start with the Millennium Drought. When did the loss start? Approach: 120 CAMELS-AUS v2.03 catchments, AGCD and SILO rain and a fixed long-record GHCN-Daily gauge network, a two-way panel model that gives a common annual runoff-efficiency profile without a calibration window, step and trend shapes with AR(1) errors and BIC, and 2-degree cell bootstraps. The plan was written first; the state split and all mechanism checks are post hoc. Results: for the pooled region, the planned test preferred a gradual decline (BIC difference -15.0, 95% interval -20.0 to -2.9), but not with gauge rain (-3.7, -10.7 to +10.1) or with a later start year. The pooled region mixes two shapes. Victoria (71 catchments) was flat in about 1957-1996 and then fell in one 1997-1998 step (step beyond trend -0.62 to -0.94 SD in three rain sources; BIC favours the step by +6 to +10). New South Wales and ACT (39) declined gradually from the 1950s; in 1985-1996 runoff was already 20-22% (42-65 mm/yr) below the 1952-1970 relation, 65-81% of the 2010-2021 loss, with no extra 1997 step. In synthetic data the method separated the two shapes. Victorian water tables (published regional series) fell gradually and reached only half of their 2001-2009 level in 1998-2000, when runoff efficiency had already reached 80-95% of its deficit. Heavy rain, wet days, the IPO phase, rain memory and PET did not change the shapes; temperature weakened the NSW shape test, but the pre-1997 NSW deficit stayed. Conclusion: the Victorian loss is an abrupt drought-time step that came before most of the groundwater fall; most of the NSW loss came before 1997 and needs a slow, non-drought cause. Limitations: post hoc split, small gauge sets, few catchments before 1960, no land-use or farm-dam time series, regional bores only.
